writeup.headline: Omnicom rates Hold: IPG-boosted growth and low absolute multiples offset by thin margins, dilution and weak trend.
writeup.thesis: Omnicom scores 61, a Hold, 4 points below the Buy band. Growth scores 82 on TTM revenue growth of 54.1% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 59.1% year on year, largely reflecting the Interpublic acquisition, though growth slowed by 4.3 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 80 because the absolute multiples are low (P/S of 0.9x, P/FCF of 7.4x, FCF yield 8.5 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield), while against its own history it sits near the middle: P/S is cheaper than at every one of the last 61 month-ends, but EV/EBIT is more expensive than at 52 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality is the main drag at 38, with a 12.6% gross margin, 6.4% operating margin and diluted share count up 41.3% year on year, and the trend score of 43 reflects a price 12.6% below its 52-week high and shares 4.8 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. News is mildly positive, with a Q3 beat and management saying it is on track for $900 million in IPG cost synergies in 2026.
key_risks: Delivery of the $900 million IPG cost synergies falls short, leaving the 6.4% operating margin thin
Heavy dilution: diluted share count up 41.3% year on year from the deal
Debt load with net debt at 2.17x FCF and cash covering 0.38x of debt
Traditional advertising still down mid-single digits, and growth will slow sharply once the acquisition laps
Weak share-price trend, with the stock below its 50-day and 200-day averages and lagging SPY and QQQ
what_would_change: A 4-point gain in the score would move it to Buy, for example from a better trend score as the shares regain their 50-day and 200-day averages
Margin improvement from synergies lifting the quality score from 38 would push toward Buy
A drop of 17 points would be needed for Sell, such as growth fading after the IPG anniversary combined with negative guidance or analyst news
EV/EBIT staying more expensive than its history while synergies disappoint would weigh on the valuation score
